author: Detroit City Wire
title: Fox Theatre hosts 2026 PWHL Draft as Detroit welcomes new women's hockey team
text:
Fox Theatre hosts 2026 PWHL Draft as Detroit welcomes new women’s hockey team
The Fox Theatre in Detroit hosted the 2026 Professional Women’s Hockey League Draft on June 24, bringing together prospects, fans, and guests from across the country for an evening focused on women’s hockey.
Ben Chiarot said, “This is Hockeytown. The Ilitches have been unbelievable supporters of sports in this city for a long time. It’s only fitting that they’d be doing the same for the women’s hockey team.” The event began with fan activities at the PWHL Fan Draft Zone on Columbia Street before Caroline Harvey was selected first overall by the Vancouver Goldeneyes. Fans watched as prospects walked the Purple Carpet outside of Fox Theatre and executives representing each of the league's 12 teams gathered inside.
Seventy-two players were drafted over six rounds, including three Michigan natives: Kristen Simms to Toronto Sceptres at No. 8 overall, Casey Borgiel to PWHL Detroit at No. 22 overall, and Elyssa Biederman to PWHL Hamilton at No. 30 overall. Chiarot and his daughter Emmerson announced Biederman's selection live on stage.
Chiarot said about his daughter attending, “It’s great to show [Emmerson] these girls that have really dedicated themselves to something. All the discipline and work that it takes to be at something like this, so it’s really cool to bring her.”
The draft followed last month’s announcement that Ilitch Sports + Entertainment would bring a new PWHL franchise—PWHL Detroit—to begin play in the 2026-27 season with home games at Little Caesars Arena and practices at BELFOR Training Center. General Manager Manon Rhéaume added six players during the draft: four forwards, one defender, and one goalie.
Andrea Brändli became PWHL Detroit's first-ever draft pick in round two (No. 15 overall). Brändli said, “Because of [Rheaume], I’ve always wanted to be the second woman to play in the NHL. She’s had a lot of impact on my career, especially when I was young. And then talking to her…just being on a call, I felt welcome. It felt like the right place to me. It’s just why I’m so happy that it ended up like that.”
The Detroit Red Wings represent Detroit as one of National Hockey League's Original Six teams and host games downtown; they are recognized as top-performing among American franchises with eleven Stanley Cup championships throughout their history, according to their official website.
